title: Define replay inputs and canonical hashes
implementation: A private native-only df-persistence contract replays one explicitly pinned local_journey melee decision. Typed choice, policy, source/handler pins and ordered actual draws are admitted before the selected reducer runs. The reducer produces fresh AcceptedDecision semantic output and a separately reconstructed schema-1 checkpoint from the narrow retained prestate. The contract compares typed choice/draw/decision records, complete encoded checkpoint bytes, and SHA-256. It also refuses missing inputs and unsupported selected revisions without changing the original checkpoint or draw records.

positive: An admitted codec-2/schema-1 checkpoint survives native decode and exact re-encode.

A bounded selected prestate and recorded AcceptedChoice, AcceptedDecision policy/output, and ordered ActualDraw records are re-admitted; local_journey::resolve_melee independently reconstructs accepted records and the final Checkpoint.
The reconstructed accepted typed choice/draw/decision records, complete final encoded bytes, and SHA-256 equal the recorded accepted checkpoint.
Choice, ordered draw values, policy, source/handler/content/build pin changes alter encoded bytes/hash; a semantic-output-byte-only perturbation also changes the hash.
A native test prints the actually computed checkpoint digest and its codec/schema/source/handler/policy identity; Root retains the value in this artifact after its repaired-source run.
The standard SHA-256 abc vector is asserted.
With the same recorded miss draw and bounded prestate, Graze and no-Graze independently replay to different accepted semantic outputs.
refusals: Missing choice, decision, or draws -> private typed refusal before reducer invocation; empty draws are rejected before indexing.
Unknown source revision, handler/source-manifest pin, policy revision, and unsupported mastery choice -> private typed refusal before reduction.
Mismatched draw source/order/type/value or count -> private typed refusal with no partial checkpoint.
Wrong codec, unsupported model schema, truncated/malformed/trailing document, stale basis, foreign pins, and capacity -> existing typed codec/checkpoint refusal.
Missing accepted choice, decision, or draws in a reconstructed checkpoint and explicit redacted/unavailable recovery markers return typed refusals; removed payload is not reconstructed.
Every refusal preserves the caller's original checkpoint and supplied draw records.
Unknown mastery choices, unsupported policy revisions, and unsupported source references are refused before comparing accepted records or invoking the selected reducer.

Full 2024 rules coverage, production registered-handler replay, provider/RNG fallback, browser, PostgreSQL, and physical durability behavior.
